To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the seismic performance of RC frame structures can be enhanced through the use of infill masonry walls, which reduce the seismic demand and the probability of collapse.
masonry infill can drastically reduce seismic capacity of RC frame structure during both main event and aftershocks.
the proposed double incremental dynamic analysis is able to capture the beneficial effect of masonry infills on the seismic response of RC frames during mainshock and aftershock events.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new approach to assess seismic vulnerability of RC frame buildings with masonry infills, which can be useful for risk analysis and mitigation purposes in the context of seismic risk assessment and seismic design of existing buildings.

the development of a methodology for the seismic fragility assessment of masonry infill RC frames subjected to mainshock-aftershock sequences, based on the use of a double incremental dynamic (D IDA), a limit state function and a fiber section model.

the seismic response assessment of RC structures, and in particular with the evaluation of the effects of infilled frames, which are very common in many countries, including Italy, and are usually not considered in the seismic assessment of RC structures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
infills are not always beneficial, but they may be if they do not lead to a collapse of the structure.
the presence of infills is beneficial, provided that the RC frame is properly designed.

masonry infill walls are not always a positive factor for the seismic response of RC structures, but their presence can be beneficial if the RC members are designed with adequate capacity to support additional shear demands due to frame infill interaction, and to avoid sudden failures which otherwise can occur.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the presence of masonry infills in RC frame structures may significantly improve the seismic performance, especially in the case of mainshock/after shock sequences, and that the proposed framework is able to capture this behavior.

masonry infilled RC frames are able to withstand mainshock/after shock sequences and that the residual capacity of RC frames with masonry infills is significantly higher than that of bare RC frames, even for low intensity earthquakes.
infill panels can be considered as an efficient seismic protection strategy, but the structural system should be designed and detailed accordingly to avoid shear failures in RC members.
The main takeaway from our work is that
infills may be a viable and cost effective solution for seismic retrofit of RC structures.
the D IDA approach can be used to assess residual capacity of infilled frame systems and to identify the most vulnerable structural members, which are those with the lowest residual capacity.
infilled frames can be considered as a viable solution for improving the seismic resilience of existing RC frame structures.
